subject: Pilot hosting decision for FastCart — throughput & tail-latency tradeoffs
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex@fastcart.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: Samira Khan <samira@fastcart.com>
Date: 2026-10-27T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot hosting decision for FastCart — throughput & tail-latency tradeoffs

Hi Olga / Ben,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the data we promised to share. Attached is our QPS profile (fastcart-qps-profile.csv) and a short network requirements doc. Key points: 

- Peak traffic: 650 req/sec sustained, short bursts up to ~1,200 req/sec during promotions
- Typical request payload: ~35-50 tokens (avg ~42 tokens)
- Tail latency target: 95th <= 180ms end-to-end for inference (from request to token stream start)
- Data residency: US-only; we may need VPC connectivity for PCI-scope logs later in the pilot
- Retention: logs/outputs retained for 30 days for debugging; audit logs required longer term

We need a recommendation: start on Hosted API to move fast, or go straight to Dedicated reserved capacity? Our preferences: fast time-to-value but not willing to miss SLAs during big promotions.

Can you outline a pilot plan and what test profile you need from us? We can target a pilot week the week of Nov 9 (preferred) — let me know available windows.

Thanks,
Alex Rivera
Head of Engineering, FastCart
Attachments: fastcart-qps-profile.csv (text/csv), fastcart-network-reqs.pdf (pdf)
From: olga_petrov@redwood.com <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@fastcart.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-27T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot hosting decision for FastCart — throughput & tail-latency tradeoffs

Alex — great notes and thanks for the files. Attaching a short worksheet (redwood-dedicated-sla-worksheet.xlsx) that outlines the testing matrix I suggest. High-level recommendation and rationale below.

Recommendation (two-stage pilot)
1) Short Hosted API validation (2–3 days): run a focused benchmark using the exact QPS profile you attached (sustained 600–700 RPS, 2x bursts to 1,200 for 5–10 minutes). Purpose: validate 95th latency under production payloads and measure token-cost. Hosted API gives fastest path to start without infra onboarding.

2) Move to a Dedicated reserved pool for production if 1) shows consistent throughput need and cost sensitivity. Dedicated gives predictable tail latency under sustained load and direct control over autoscaling windows. Given your burst patterns around promotions, Dedicated can be configured with burst capacity and warm pools.

Why not Private/VPC immediately?
- Private VPC/on-prem makes sense later for full PCI scoping and when you need customer-managed networking. For the pilot and initial production we recommend Hosted -> Dedicated. That minimizes time-to-value while keeping a migration path.

Suggested test plan (I will coordinate with Ben and Priyom):
- Synthetic benchmark: replay fastcart-qps-profile.csv for 45 minutes (600–700 RPS sustained) + two 10-minute bursts at 1,200 RPS.
- Metrics to capture: 95th latency, p99 latency, token/sec, instance GPU utilization, error rates.
- Success criteria: 95th <= 180ms, p99 < 350ms, error rate < 0.5% during sustained period.
- Network prep: please confirm outbound whitelists and provide an internal IP block for VPC peering when/if we move to Dedicated (see attached network-reqs.pdf).

Next steps (owners & dates)
- Today (Olga): send SLA worksheet and benchmark matrix (attached).
- By 2026-11-02 (FastCart): confirm pilot week and provide a stable test client + IP whitelist details.
- 2026-11-09 (Redwood + FastCart): run hosted validation benchmark (Ben to schedule).
- Post-validation (Redwood): we’ll provide a cost/latency readout and a Dedicated sizing recommendation (Priyom will draft).

If you’re comfortable, I recommend we keep the pilot on Hosted API for validation. If results show the need for predictable sustained throughput with tight tails, we’ll size a Dedicated pool and plan the cutover.

Thanks — Ben and Priyom are looped in to handle scheduling and the benchmark run.

—
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Thanks Olga / Ben — Nov 9 10:00 PT works for us. A couple quick clarifications before the run: 

1) VPC during pilot: can we get at least a transient VPC peering for logs to flow to our SIEM? We understand a full Private deployment isn’t necessary yet, but we need to capture logs for PCI auditing during the tests.

2) Retention and audit logs: during the pilot we want 30-day retention for payload logs and separate audit logs retained for 1 year. Is that supported on Hosted for the duration of the pilot?

3) Narrow question on Dedicated sizing: if the validation shows sustained 700 RPS with the token profile we shared, roughly what Dedicated pool size should we expect (ballpark GPU count) and how long to provision? A short estimate is fine; we just need planning numbers.

We’ll send the test client repo and IP whitelist by EOD Oct 31. Also attaching an updated network-reqs.pdf with our SIEM endpoints.

Alex Rivera
Head of Engineering, FastCart
